"Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation, and the rich in his: humiliation, because like a flower of the grass he will pass away" (1:9–10) is in 10.14 The proud; brought low, the lowly raised (Where the boast goes, claim C-182). 1:11 only finishes the figure:; "So also will the rich man fade away in the midst of his pursuits." Nothing new.

Ezekiel 21:26: already carried. It is in the same 10.14 list. The passage (21:25–27) is said to: "profane wicked one, prince of Israel": "Remove the turban and take off the crown. Things shall not; remain as they are." It is a word of judgment on a ruler, not an inner act. Nothing new.

The reversal is the same one 10.14 lists. Two; things are new:; its purpose: "shall know that I am the Lord"; its certainty: "I have spoken, and I will do it".

findings.text: The passage (5:8–16) is Eliphaz's counsel: "As for me, I would seek God" (5:8). It ends "So the poor: have hope, and injustice shuts her mouth" (5:16). The words match what the rest of Scripture says of; the lowly raised. But the book's practice with Job's friends is to name the speaker, and to note that; God's verdict stands over them: "you have not spoken of me what is right" (Job 42:7). This is done; for Bildad in Ch 2 and 10.12 (claim C-153). So if it is used at all, it must carry that frame; "those who mourn are lifted to safety" and "the poor have hope" are inner-being words: mourning; and hope.
For OT-97.17 itself: nothing new for M09. Isa 57:15, Jam 1:9 and Eze 21:26 are already in 10.14,: and the M18 part was superseded by OT-105. The item can be closed as carried.
